1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
30		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
31	
32		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
33		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
34	)
35	
36	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
37	type Column[T any] struct {
38		Title string
39		// MinWidth is what the column asks for. It is a request, not a guarantee:
40		// when the terminal is too narrow for every request, the shortfall is
41		// shared out rather than each column defending its own floor.
42		MinWidth int
43		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over. 0 keeps it at
44		// MinWidth; the leftover is split between the flexible ones by weight.
45		Flex int
46		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: bubbles/table
47		// truncates with runewidth, which does not understand ANSI, so a styled
48		// string is cut mid-escape and bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122).
49		// Taking a string rather than a styled value is what makes that
50		// unexpressible here.
51		Cell func(T) string
52		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
53		// `.` skips it.
54		Less func(a, b T) bool
55		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
56		// not participate.
57		Search func(T) string
58	}
59	
60	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
61	type Config[T any] struct {
62		Columns []Column[T]
63		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
64		Tokens []components.FilterToken
65		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
66		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
67		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
68		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
69		SortColumn int
70		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
71		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
72		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
73		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
74		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
75		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
76	}
77	
78	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
79	type Model[T any] struct {
80		cfg   Config[T]
81		table table.Model
82		bar   components.FilterBar
83	
84		items []T
85		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
86		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
87		// ordering while the screen shows another.
88		visible []T
89	
90		sortColumn int
91		sortDesc   bool

95	// New builds a table from its configuration.
96	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
97		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
98		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
99			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
100		}
101		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
102		t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
103	
104		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
105		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
106			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
107		}

109		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn}
110		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
111		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
112		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
113		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
114		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
115			m.sortColumn = -1
116		}

120	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
121	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
122	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
123	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
124	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
125		m.items = items

127	}

130	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }

135	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is

138		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
139		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
140			var zero T

206	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
207	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
208	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
209	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
210		m.width = width
211		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, availableFor(width, len(m.cfg.Columns)))
212	
213		cols := m.table.Columns()
214		for i := range cols {
215			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
216			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)

226	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
227	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
228		if i != m.sortColumn {
229			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
230		}
231		if m.sortDesc {
232			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + " ▼"
233		}
234		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + " ▲"

237	// CycleSort advances the sort: ascending, descending, then on to the next
238	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
239	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
240	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
241		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
242		if len(sortable) == 0 {
243			return
244		}
245		switch {
246		case m.sortColumn < 0:
247			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = sortable[0], false
248		case !m.sortDesc:
249			m.sortDesc = true
250		default:
251			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = m.nextSortable(sortable), false
252		}
253		m.rebuild()
254		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
255	}
256	
257	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
258	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
259	//
260	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
261	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
262	// a branch nothing can ever check.
263	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
264		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
265			return sortable[at+1]
266		}
267		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
268			return -1
269		}
270		return sortable[0]
271	}

274		var out []int
275		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
276			if c.Less != nil {

287	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,

289	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.

311		case ".":
312			m.CycleSort()
313		case "up", "k":

345	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
346		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
347	
348		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))

353			}
354			rows[i] = cells

359		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
360		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
361		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
362		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
363		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
364		case len(rows) == 0:
365			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
366			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
367			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
368			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
369		case cursor >= len(rows):
370			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
371		case cursor < 0:
372			m.table.SetCursor(0)
373		}
374		m.applyStyles()
375	}

378	func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
379		if !m.table.Focused() {
380			return // Blur owns the styles until Focus takes them back
381		}
382		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
383		if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok && m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
384			styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
385		}
386		// Pin the selected row to the full content width. Column widths are counted
387		// in cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
388		// counts, so the highlight otherwise stops short of the right border by
389		// however much the row's icons disagreed. Padding to a width the row can
390		// never exceed is a no-op when they agree.
391		if m.width > 2 {
392			styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(m.width - 2)
393		}
394		m.table.SetStyles(styles)
395	}

398	func (m *Model[T]) filtered() []T {
399		query := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.bar.SearchQuery()))
400		active := m.activeTokens()
401	
402		out := make([]T, 0, len(m.items))
403		for _, item := range m.items {
404			if m.cfg.TokenMatch != nil && !m.cfg.TokenMatch(item, active) {
405				continue
406			}
407			if query != "" && !m.matchesQuery(item, query) {
408				continue
409			}
410			out = append(out, item)
411		}
412		return out
413	}

416		active := make(map[string]bool, len(m.cfg.Tokens))
417		for _, tok := range m.cfg.Tokens {

426	// the row as a whole.
427	//
428	// The row-level pass is what keeps a query spanning two fields — "tcp 22" over a
429	// ports list — working: netdiag matched against a joined haystack while the
430	// other four filter loops matched per field, and per field alone would have
431	// quietly dropped those matches on migration. Matching both ways is a superset
432	// of either, so no view loses anything and they all gain the same thing.
433	func (m *Model[T]) matchesQuery(item T, query string) bool {
434		var joined strings.Builder
435		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
436			if c.Search == nil {
437				continue
438			}
439			value := c.Search(item)
440			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), query) {
441				return true
442			}
443			if joined.Len() > 0 {
444				joined.WriteByte(' ')
445			}
446			joined.WriteString(value)
447		}
448		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(joined.String()), query)
449	}
450	
451	// sorted orders the visible slice. SliceStable, because sort.Slice is not and
452	// two rows equal on the sort column would otherwise swap between rebuilds.
453	func (m *Model[T]) sorted(items []T) []T {
454		if m.sortColumn < 0 {
455			return items
456		}
457		less := m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less // never nil — see New
458		desc := m.sortDesc
459		sort.SliceStable(items, func(i, j int) bool {
460			if desc {
461				return less(items[j], items[i])
462			}
463			return less(items[i], items[j])
464		})
465		return items
466	}

Phase 2 of the configuration-view plan is done and up as **[PR #44](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/44)**.

## What shipped

`:sec` now opens on an **inventory** of everything the current context has scanned — one `datatable` over both scan caches (images and repositories), sorted by CRITICAL descending. `enter` opens a row's stored findings, `ctrl+s` rescans one, `ctrl+a` purges and rescans all, `ctrl+r` reloads.

The inventory runs its own scans rather than delegating back to the originating view: with the options now in the config, there is nothing left to carry across.

## Three things the plan didn't anticipate

- **`ctrl+a` purges the counts, not the rows.** Here the rows *are* the cache, unlike the images tab where they come from Docker — purging them would empty the view for the length of the scans and lose the targets on a close. A purged row prints `-`, not `0`.
- **A reload has to keep an in-flight scan's marker**, or a refresh landing mid-rescan clears the spinner and the row looks settled while its scan is still running.
- **`InventoryScanFinishedMsg` needs routing to the security view wherever the user is.** The router forwards everything else to the active view only, so leaving the view mid-rescan would have left a row spinning for the life of the view. `routeToOCIImagesView` already existed for exactly this.

I also added `SortDesc` to `datatable.Config` — the plan asks for CRITICAL-descending on open and the component could only express ascending.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues) and the full suite are green. Coverage went **up**: `internal/ui/security` 85.6% → 85.9%, project total 81.3% → 81.4% (measured against `main` by stashing). I confirmed each new invariant bites by removing its implementation and watching the specific test fail — purge, reload marker, spinner chain, esc-reload, routing, and both `SortDesc` cases.

## Two things to note

The form is **not** deleted — that is phase 3, and it stays reachable through `NewWithTarget`/`NewWithImageTarget`. Its tests still pass and still describe it; I made `newTestModel` ask for `StateInput` explicitly rather than assume it.

I have not run the TUI itself — the test plan in the PR leaves three manual checks unticked (the rows on a real context, leaving mid-rescan, and the empty state). Everything asserted above is from the automated suite.
